time: A continuous, irreversible process in which events occur from the past, through the present, and into the future.
year: A period of 365 or 366 days, typically measured from January 1 to December 31.
people: Human beings in general or collectively.
way: A method, style, or manner of doing something.
day: A 24-hour period, typically from midnight to midnight.
thing: An object or item, or a concept or idea.
life: The existence of living organisms, characterized by growth, reproduction, and continual change.
child: A young human being, typically under the age of 18.
world: The planet Earth or the entirety of human society and civilization.
school: A place where education is provided to students.
state: A political entity or government, or a condition or mode of being.
family: A group of individuals related by blood, marriage, or other close ties.
student: A person who is learning at an educational institution.
group: A collection of individuals or things considered together.
country: A nation with its own government, borders, and sovereignty.
problem: A question or situation requiring a solution.
hand: The part of the body at the end of the arm, used for grasping and manipulating objects.
part: A portion or component of a whole.
case: An occurrence or situation, often used to describe an instance requiring investigation.
company: A business or organization involved in commercial activities.
system: A set of connected things or parts that work together as a whole.
program: A planned series of events or activities, often in the form of a software application.
question: An inquiry or query to gain information.
work: The effort or labor done to achieve a particular result.
government: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.
number: A mathematical value or a figure used for counting.
night: The time of day when it is dark, typically from sunset to sunrise.
point: A specific location or idea; a sharp end or tip.
home: A place where one lives, often associated with comfort and family.
water: A clear, colorless, odorless liquid essential for life.
room: A space or area within a building, typically enclosed by walls.
area: A specific region or space, often measured in terms of square units.
money: A medium of exchange, typically in the form of coins and banknotes.
story: A narrative or account of events, real or fictional.
fact: A true, verifiable piece of information.
month: A unit of time, typically one of the 12 divisions of a year.
lot: A large amount or quantity; also refers to a piece of land.
right: A moral or legal entitlement; or the opposite of left.
study: The process of learning or acquiring knowledge.
book: A set of written or printed pages, typically bound together, forming a work of literature or information.
job: A paid position of employment or work.
word: A unit of language that has meaning and can stand alone.
business: A commercial activity or enterprise aimed at making a profit.
issue: A problem, concern, or subject for discussion.
side: A particular aspect or part of something; also refers to a position in a conflict.
kind: A type, sort, or variety; also refers to being compassionate and considerate.
head: The topmost part of the body, containing the brain, eyes, ears, and mouth.
house: A building designed for people to live in.
service: An act of providing help or a service to others.
friend: A person with whom one has a close and supportive relationship.
power: The ability to influence or control others; also refers to energy or force.
hour: A unit of time, equal to 60 minutes.
game: A structured activity or competition, often involving rules and scoring.
line: A long, narrow mark or a row of people or objects.
end: The point at which something finishes or ceases.
member: A person who belongs to a group or organization.
law: A system of rules created and enforced by government or social institutions.
car: A vehicle used for transporting people and goods.
city: A large and densely populated urban area.
community: A group of people living in the same area or sharing common interests.
name: A word or term by which a person or thing is known.
president: The elected head of a republic, or leader of a company or organization.
team: A group of individuals working together toward a common goal.
minute: A unit of time, equal to 60 seconds.
idea: A thought, concept, or plan formed in the mind.
kid: An informal term for a child.
body: The physical structure of a person or organism.
information: Data or knowledge that is communicated.
back: The rear part of something; also refers to returning to a previous position.
face: The front part of the head, including the eyes, nose, and mouth.
others: Refers to people or things besides oneself.
level: A position or rank on a scale; also refers to a flat or even surface.
office: A place where business or professional work is carried out.
door: A movable barrier used to close or open an entryway.
health: The state of being free from illness or injury.
art: Creative work or expression, often in visual, musical, or literary forms.
war: A state of armed conflict between different countries or groups.
history: The study of past events or the record of those events.
party: A social gathering or a political organization.
result: The outcome or effect of a particular action or event.
change: The process of becoming different or undergoing transformation.
morning: The early part of the day, typically from dawn until noon.
reason: A cause or explanation for something.
research: The systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources to establish facts.
girl: A female child or young woman.
guy: An informal term for a man or person.
air: The invisible mixture of gases that makes up the Earth's atmosphere.
teacher: A person who educates or instructs others, typically in a school setting.
force: Strength or energy exerted to make something happen; or a group that exerts power or control.
education: The process of teaching, learning, and acquiring knowledge and skills.
